title: Juno
summary: Juno is a solar-powered orbiter sent to study Jupiter's composition, gravity field, magnetic field, and polar magnetosphere from a highly elliptical, near-polar orbit. It followed Galileo as only the second dedicated orbiter mission to Jupiter, and it is the first outer-planet mission to rely on solar panels rather than a nuclear power source, made possible by three large solar arrays that also give the spacecraft its distinctive windmill-like shape. Juno reached Jupiter after an Earth flyby gravity assist that boosted its speed on the way out.

instruments.name: Microwave Radiometer (MWR)
instruments.purpose: Probes below the visible cloud tops to measure water abundance and atmospheric structure

instruments.name: Jovian Infrared Auroral Mapper (JIRAM)
instruments.purpose: Images auroras and atmospheric heat in infrared wavelengths

instruments.name: Magnetometer (MAG)
instruments.purpose: Maps the planet's magnetic field in fine detail

instruments.name: JunoCam
instruments.purpose: Visible-light camera that returns wide-angle images, including many chosen with public input

timeline.event: Launch from Cape Canaveral aboard an Atlas V rocket
Earth gravity-assist flyby on the outbound trajectory
Close flyby of the Great Red Spot
Mission extended to include flybys of Ganymede, Europa, and Io
Close flyby of the volcanic moon Io

discoveries: Jupiter's interior mixes heavy elements more evenly than earlier models predicted
Massive polar cyclones arranged in geometric clusters at each pole
The Great Red Spot extends far deeper into the atmosphere than previously known
notes: Juno carries three small LEGO figurines (Galileo Galilei, and the Roman gods Jupiter and Juno) as a public-outreach feature riding alongside the science payload. The mission has been repeatedly extended past its original end date.
